facts.statement: Coloradisaurus is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur.
facts.quote: Coloradisaurus (meaning "Los Colorados lizard") is a genus of massospondylid sauropodomorph dinosaur.

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus lived during the Late Triassic period in what is now La Rioja Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Triassic period (Norian stage) in what is now La Rioja Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus is known from two specimens found in the Los Colorados Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from two specimens collected from the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Coloradisaurus were discovered in 1971 at the La Esquina locality in Argentina.
facts.quote: All material of Coloradisaurus was discovered in 1971 at the La Esquina locality in the upper section of the Los Colorados Formation near Pagancillo, La Rioja Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: The expedition that found Coloradisaurus was organized by the Fundación Miguel Lillo with financial support from the National Council of Scientific and Technical Research.
facts.quote: La expedición que realizó el hallazgo fue organizada por la Fundación Miguel Lillo, con el soporte financiero de Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas.

facts.statement: Martín Vince, Juan C. Leal, Tomás H. Fasola, and José F. Bonaparte participated in the discovery of Coloradisaurus.
facts.quote: Martín Vince, Juan C. Leal, Tomás H. Fasola y José F. Bonaparte participaron en esta.

facts.statement: The holotype of Coloradisaurus is estimated to have been 3 meters long and weighed 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype individual has been estimated to have been 3 m (10 ft) long with a mass of 70 kg (150 lb).

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus was a medium-sized prosauropod that could reach 4 meters in length, 2 meters in height, and weigh about 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: Coloradisaurus fue un prósauropodo de tamaño medio que llegó a medir 4 metros de largo, 2 de alto y unos 100 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus had a high, short head with large eye orbits.
facts.quote: La cabeza es alta y corta con órbitas oculares grandes.

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 213 million years ago.
facts.quote: The top of the Los Colorados Formation has been dated to 213 Ma, which would place Coloradisaurus in the Norian stage of the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Coloradisaurus lived in South America during the Late Triassic, approximately 218 to 210 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 218 y 210 millones de años, en el Noriense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Coloradisaurus is estimated to be between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Modern consensus classifies Coloradisaurus as a massospondylid closely related to Lufengosaurus and Glacialisaurus.
facts.quote: Subsequent analyses such as Yates et al. (2010), Apaldetti et al. (2013; 2014), Wang et al. (2017), and Müller (2020) have reached the consensus that Coloradisaurus is a massospondylid most closely related to Lufengosaurus and Glacialisaurus.

facts.statement: It is possible that Coloradisaurus is an adult specimen of Mussaurus.
facts.quote: Existe la posibilidad que Coloradisaurus sea un ejemplar adulto de Mussaurus.

facts.statement: Recent findings suggest Coloradisaurus is the sister taxon of Lufengosaurus and both clearly belong to Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Los últimos hallazgos sugieren que Coloradisaurus es el taxón hermano de Lufengosaurus y ambos pertenecen claramente a Massospondylidae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses found Coloradisaurus to be basal to Glacialisaurus, forming a clade with Lufengosaurus within Massospondylidae.
facts.quote: Los análisis cladisticos por Yates en 200, Yates et al. en 2010 y 2011 y Novas et al. 2011 encontraron que Coloradisaurus es basal al Glacialisaurus formando un clado con Lufengosaurus dentro de Massospondylidae.

rejected.statement: Some analyses have recovered Coloradisaurus in a polytomy with other basal sauropodomorphs or as a massospondylid, creating debate about its exact placement.
rejected.quote: However, the analyses of Benton et al. (2000) and Yates (2003) recovered it in a polytomy with other basal sauropodomorphs or as a massospondylid, respectively.
